headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq at roughly a $2 trillion value
dek: Shares opened 34% above the IPO price, per CNBC and Fortune.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What happened
body: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, per CNBC Technology and Fortune.
Shares opened at $111.50, up 34% from the IPO price (CNBC Technology).

points.t: $83 a share, above the range (CNBC Technology).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: The numbers
body: Revenue was $33.24 billion in nine months, up roughly 1,200% (CNBC Technology).
The net loss was $104 billion, tied to convertible notes and derivatives (Fortune).

stat.cap: raised in the biggest IPO (CNBC Technology)

items.t: Still private, not expected before 2027 (CNBC Technology).
Senators criticized the lack of regulation.

caption.hook: Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq and shares opened 34% above the IPO price.
body: Per CNBC Technology and Fortune, the maker of Claude began trading under the ticker ANT and opened at $111.50, pushing its market value to roughly $2 trillion. The IPO was priced at $83 a share, above the $70-to-$78 range.

The offering raised $81.3 billion, the largest on record by funds raised, ahead of SpaceX's $75 billion, per CNBC Technology. The company posted $33.24 billion in revenue over nine months but a $104 billion net loss, attributed mostly to accounting changes, per Fortune.
